anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiology data into BIDS, used in dataset curation, not a paper describing this EEG-fMRI dataset.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a data-organization standard extension that this dataset's BIDS formatting uses; it does not describe this EEG-fMRI experience-sampling dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Data were acquired on a 3T Siemens MAGNETOM Prisma with a 64-channel head coil. Acquisition included an MPRAGE T1-weighted scan, a B0 field map, and multiband gradient-echo EPI BOLD scans (TR 2000 ms, 2 mm isotropic voxels). EEG was recorded with a Brain Products MR-compatible system (BrainAmp MRPlus, BrainCap MR with 31 EEG channels, 4 carbon wire loops, and 1 ECG channel) at 5 kHz. MRI TR markers were recorded in the EEG data for synchronization. Each participant completed two sessions with one GradCPT run and three resting-state experience-sampling runs.
